original_interpretation: WSTS describes itself as a non-profit organization of semiconductor product companies founded in 1986 and as the industry's only source for monthly industry shipment statistics.
evidence_found: "World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS) was founded in 1986 as a non-profit organization of semiconductor product companies and is the industry's only source for monthly industry shipment statistics." (About WSTS, last page of Spring 2026 release)
notes: Self-description, correctly typed reported_claim. Same boilerplate in the Autumn 2025 and Spring 2025 releases.

original_interpretation: WSTS's published market forecast tables use four regions (Americas, Europe, Japan, Asia Pacific), in which China is not shown separately.
evidence_found: WSTS Spring 2026 release (2 June 2026), "WSTS Forecast Summary" table (cols 2025 2026 2027 | growth 2025 2026 2027, "Amounts in US$M") rows: "Americas", "Europe", "Japan", "Asia Pacific", "Total World - $M"; no China row. Product Classification 2021 §1(c): Market Forecasts use "classification of 4 regions of the world market defined for the years 2013 and before."
notes: The four regions add up to Total World (256,476+54,694+44,723+439,747=795,640), so China sits inside Asia Pacific.

original_interpretation: WSTS reported the 2025 world semiconductor market at US$795.6 billion, up 26.2% from 2024.
evidence_found: WSTS Spring 2026 release (2 June 2026), "WSTS Forecast Summary" table (cols 2025 2026 2027 | growth 2025 2026 2027, "Amounts in US$M"): "Total World - $M 795,640 1,511,248 1,913,683 26.2 89.9 26.6"

original_interpretation: In June 2026 WSTS forecast the world semiconductor market to grow 90% in 2026 to US$1.51 trillion.
evidence_found: "the global semiconductor market is now projected to grow 90 percent in 2026, reaching USD 1.51 trillion." (Spring 2026 release p.1); table "Total World - $M ... 1,511,248 ... 89.9"
notes: Correct as a dated Spring 2026 forecast. WSTS's Aug 2026 Q2 release (SRC-0245) recalculated 2026 at "1,655 billion US dollars ... approximately 108 percent" (CLM-0733) but says "these are not new forecast values", so Spring 2026 is still WSTS's latest official forecast. The Autumn 2026 forecast is due around Dec 2026.

original_interpretation: WSTS defines reportable semiconductor products as either packaged/encapsulated die or chips that are tested and marked, or unencapsulated die, chips or wafers that have been tested to product specifications.
evidence_found: "Semiconductor Products are defined in two forms: 1. Packaged or encapsulated die or chips with leads or contacts, which are tested and marked (or identified) to meet the product specifications (finished products). 2. Die, chips or wafers, which have not been encapsulated but have been tested to meet the product specifications and are identified by the container..." (§2.2, p.4)
notes: Locator fix: §2.2 is on p.4, not p.3. Source is the 2021 issue (dated 10 Dec 2020). It says there was no change from 2020; no later public issue was found.

original_interpretation: WSTS counts chip development charges such as non-recurring engineering (NRE) charges for custom and semi-custom devices as part of reported semiconductor value.
evidence_found: "Chip development charges, such as non-recurring engineering (NRE) charges for custom and semi-custom devices, are part of the value to be reported." (§3.4.1 Analog, p.8). Gate Arrays/Standard Cells (§L2b/L2c, pp.17-18): "The manufacturer reports billings including Non Recurring Engineering (NRE) charges..." but "Charges for NRE or Computer Aided Design tools used for feasibility or research studies are not to be reported."
correction: The sentence quoted is in the Analog section, not a general rule. Equivalent NRE-inclusion rules appear for MOS Gate Arrays and Standard Cells. NRE for feasibility or research studies, and third-party design-centre charges, are explicitly excluded.

original_interpretation: The WSTS classification has four top-level product groups: discretes, optoelectronics, sensors and actuators, and integrated circuits; integrated circuits are split into analog, MOS micro, logic and memory.
evidence_found: Contents: "3.1. Discretes", "3.2. Optoelectronics", "3.3. Sensors and Actuators", "3.4. Integrated Circuits" with "3.4.1. Analog", "3.4.2. MOS Micro", "3.4.3. Total Logic (MOS & Bipolar)", "3.4.4. MOS Memory"; §3.5 "T99 Total Semiconductor... equals the total of subtotals S3, F99, H99 and S2." (pp.1, 25)
notes: §3.4.5 'Total Application Specific ICs' (Q99) is a cross-cutting aggregate, not a fifth IC group, so the four-way IC split holds.

original_interpretation: In the WSTS classification, MOS Micro comprises microprocessors (MPU), microcontrollers (MCU) and digital signal processors (DSP), and Memory comprises DRAM, SRAM, flash and ROM/EPROM types.
evidence_found: §3.4.2 (p.13): "This category contains three subcategories, i.e. MOS Microprocessor (MPU) (code P1), MOS Microcontroller (MCU) (code P2), and Digital Signal Processor (DSP) (code P4)." §3.4.4 (p.22): "MOS Memory contains the following subcategories; DRAM (M1) SRAM (M2) Mask Programmable ROM & EPROM (M8) Flash Memory (M7) Other Memory (M6)"
correction: MOS Micro part is correct. MOS Memory also includes a fifth subcategory, Other Memory (M6): EEPROMs other than flash, FIFOs/LIFOs, EAROM, NOVRAM and memory IC cards. 'M99 Total MOS Memory. Totals of items M1, M2, M6, M7 and M8.' (p.24)

original_interpretation: WSTS optoelectronics excludes liquid crystal devices and displays and incandescent lamps, so LCD panels are outside the WSTS semiconductor market (display driver ICs are counted under logic).
evidence_found: §3.2 (p.6): "Includes displays, lamps, couplers, and other opto-sensing and emitting semiconductor devices (excludes liquid crystal devices and displays, incandescent lamps and displays, etc.)." §L3 (p.19): "MOS Display Drivers – Devices specifically designed to control and drive flat panel displays such as LCD". §J4a (p.9): "Interface Logic and Amplification – line drivers, receivers, keyboard encoders, error checking circuits, and display drivers."
correction: The LCD exclusion is verified. But display drivers are not only in Logic: MOS flat-panel display drivers are Logic (L3), while analog interface display drivers are classed under Analog J4a.

original_interpretation: A company may become a WSTS member only if it at least designs and sells semiconductor products under its own trade name, and members are obliged to report their revenue data regularly to WSTS's Data Collection Agents.
evidence_found: WSTS site sidebar on the Overview page (via browser): "A company that at least designs and sells semiconductor products under its own trade name may become WSTS member." Overview body: "Membership both comprises the obligation to feed the member company's revenue data regularly into the appointed Data Collection Agents and fund the operation and services of WSTS by membership fees."
notes: The 'at least' wording supports reading this as a minimum (only-if) condition. The membership sentence is a site-wide sidebar box, not in the page body, and web_extract missed it; it was read with the browser. Members also pay membership fees.
